Jia (PM): Heads-up — big retail customer asked for a contract that ties model onboarding to reserved capacity SLAs. They want guarantees for latency + a migration window if model pins change. Can we sketch acceptance criteria?
Elaine (Product): Yikes. Do they mean every model we onboard for them must have a dedicated capacity commit? Or just tiered guarantees?
Jia (PM): They want two lanes: 1) 'Capacity-backed' (reserved Dedicated pool, SLA 99.9% uptime + p95 < 250ms) and 2) 'Standard-hosted' (best-effort, lower commit). They expect a 90-day migration window before deprecation.
Sam (Eng): For capacity-backed we need a clear perf benchmark + regression gate. What workload p50/p95 numbers are we defining? Also need to call out KV-cache warmup assumptions.
Omar (SRE): Also define expected traffic shape. If they reserve X GPUs, what concurrent QPS can we promise? We should avoid hard numbers without sizing. Suggest a couple of templates: small (1-2 A100 equiv), medium (4), large (8+).
Elaine (Product): Agreed. Proposal: acceptance = 1) perf: p95 <= 250ms at baseline seq=128 under target QPS (template-based), 2) stability: 99.9% uptime over 7-day canary, 3) quality: pass 95% of curated eval prompts (we'll reuse onboarding eval suite).
Sam (Eng): Adding: memory/kv metrics during canary (cold-start rate, cache hit ratio) — include thresholds. Also require model artifacts to be quantized/compatible with our runtime or we won't support the dedicated lane.
Jia (PM): Good. For deprecation/migration: customer asks for 90-day notice + opt-in for compatibility shim for 30 days post-deprecation. Can we support a compatibility shim? What's the cost?
Omar (SRE): Shim is possible but operationally expensive — basically dual-serving and translation layers. Recommend offering it as paid add-on (migration-assist). For standard customers, provide 90-day notice + migration playbook.
Sam (Eng): If we do a shim, we need a rollback criteria and circuit breaker. Suggest automatic fallback to pinned older model for first 2% of traffic during cutover, expand if no regressions. Keep observability hooks in Console with per-prompt diffs.
Elaine (Product): That ties into Optimize (cost toolkit) — we should include recommendations: batching, quantization level, suggested sequence caps to hit the p95 target. Also a cost split example for customers on capacity-backed lanes.
Jia (PM): Action items: 1) Eng to propose benchmark harness + perf thresholds (Sam) — due EOD Tue. 2) SRE to draft capacity templates and migration-assist cost estimate (Omar) — due Thu. 3) Product to draft contract language for 90-day notice + add-on shim (Elaine) — due Fri.
Sam (Eng): Quick note — benchmark harness will include synthetic and replay modes. Example command we'll use:
```
./bench --model=/models/customerX/v1 --seq=128 --qps=200 --warmup=300s
```
We'll output p50/p95, tokens/sec, and kv-cache-hit.
Omar (SRE): I'll map GPUs->QPS in the template and include guidance for autoscale bursts (burst buffer for 10% traffic spikes). Also flag networking egress limits if they plan multi-region.
Elaine (Product): One more ask from legal: spell out pinning TTL and renewal process. Recommend default pin TTL = 180 days with auto-renew opt-in. Add a clause for emergency rollback at our discretion for security incidents.
Jia (PM): Perfect. I'll consolidate into a one-pager for the sales team. If anyone has strong objections to the 180-day TTL or 99.9% target, speak up now.
Sam (Eng): 99.9% is OK for Dedicated if we scope availability (exclude customer-side network). 180 days seems long; can we offer 90-day opt-down for startups?
Elaine (Product): We can add tiers: enterprise default 180d, startup/SMB 90d. Put that in the one-pager.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: docs/onboarding/sla-templates v2 -> prod at 2026-03-24T09:00Z :rocket:
Jia (PM): Thanks team — merging notes. I'll post the one-pager + a short checklist in #sales-wins when ready.
